newsitem.title: GERMANY: Revised German grain intervention offers detailed.
newsitem.headline: Revised German grain intervention offers detailed.

text.p: German offers of grain in the 1996/97 (Nov/May) intervention season totalled 1,557,760 on June 30, compared with 1,677,448 a year earlier, according to revised data supplied by the agriculture ministry on Tuesday.
The total had fluctuated in the month after the May 30 deadline as some offers into intervention had been rejected, while others had been withdrawn by sellers.
The ministry said the volume was below last year because market prices had been mostly above the intervention buying-in level.
Traders and consumers had built up stocks while grain use in feed and exports had also risen from last year.
The ministry gave the following breakdown of offers in tonnes, citing official data from intervention board BLE.
A regional breakdown showed some 60 percent of the offers were made in former eastern Germany, some 20 percent in the western state of Lower Saxony and eight percent in Bavaria.
